question.text: The velocity of an object travelling along a straight line varies with time as v = (3 + 6t + 9t²) cm/s, where t is in seconds. Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The acceleration of the object at t = 3 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Its displacement during the time interval from t = 5 s to t = 8 s.

solution.approach: Differentiate the velocity for acceleration and integrate it between the two times for displacement.

steps.text: Differentiate v with respect to time to get the acceleration.
Integrate v with respect to time from t = 5 s to t = 8 s to get the displacement.
Evaluate the integral at the two limits and subtract.

common_mistakes.text: Differentiating 9t² as 9t instead of 18t gives an acceleration of 33 cm/s² at t = 3 s instead of 60 cm/s².
Subtracting the velocity at t = 5 s from the velocity at t = 8 s instead of integrating gives 369 cm instead of 1287 cm.
